name: Dynamic voltage restorer
summary: A series converter that injects a corrective voltage through a transformer to ride a sensitive load through voltage sags.
description: A dynamic voltage restorer is connected in series between the supply and a sensitive load through an injection transformer. When the supply voltage sags, a converter fed from a DC store or from the supply itself injects the missing voltage so the load sees an almost constant voltage, typically for sags lasting up to a few seconds.

Single-line diagrams show an injection transformer with its primary in series with the feeder, its secondary connected to a converter, and a DC capacitor or storage element. A bypass switch around the injection transformer allows the device to be taken out of service.

A DVR corrects sags but does not supply the load during a full outage, unlike a UPS. The symbol does not show the maximum sag depth or duration it can correct, which depends on the stored energy and converter rating.
readingNotes: The series transformer, not a shunt connection, identifies a DVR.
Check the bypass arrangement for maintenance.
drawingChecklist: State load rating, sag depth and duration corrected.
distinction: A DVR injects series voltage for sags; a STATCOM injects shunt current to support bus voltage.
